text:
Nimbus
Now downwards by the world’s attraction driven,
That tends to earth, which had upris’n to heaven;
Threatening in the mad thunder-cloud, as when
Fierce legions clash, and vanish from the plain;
Sad destiny of the troubled world! but see,
The mist is now dispersing gloriously:
And language fails us in its vain endeavour —
The spirit mounts above, and lives forever.

citation.display: Goethe, from “In Honour of Mr. Howard” (c. 1820), trans. George Soane and Sir John Bowring, Gold’s London Magazine 4.19 (July 1821), 59-63.
citation.bibliography: Goethe, Johann Wolfgang von. "In Honour of Mr. Howard." Translated by George Soane and John Bowring, Gold’s London Magazine, vol. 4, no. 19, July 1821, pp. 59–63. Written c. 1820.
citation.title: In Honour of Mr. Howard

phenomena.note: Goethe's poem on Howard's nimbus cloud, ending on the spirit rising.
